newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were epxected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle futures were called steady to 0.200 higher, livestock analysts said.
Further weakness in boxed beef prices, adequate fed cattle supplies and weak technical indications should keep pressure on live cattle futures, sources said.
Reduced demand for beef on a seasonal basis should temper packer demand for fed cattle, analysts said.
Boxed beef values on Tuesday declined another $0.13 to $0.99 per cwt Tuesday, according to the USDA.
However, fund rolling could bring uneven trade.
The "Goldman roll" started Tuesday and should continue through the week, sources said. The Goldman Sachs fund will roll their long August positions into October, sources said.
Feeder cattle may find renewed support on a rebound in the latest CME feeder cattle index and some lower corn futures indications.
Also, demand for tight feeder cattle supplies continues strong and declining interest rates also may support feeder futures, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.21 per cwt at $80.40.
